_comment: Generic reference data. Ships with the skill, replaced on every provision, reviewed in git. Nothing here is specific to a particular tank, animal or bottle - that is instance data and lives on the volume. See specs/06.

conversions.hardness_note: German degrees to ppm as CaCO3. d = ppm / 17.86.
conversions.tds_from_ec_note: A meter setting, NaCl-referenced. Not a chemical relationship - do not present it as physics.
conversions.drops_note: On a standard Seachem cap. One cap thread is about 1 mL.
conversions.hi700_note: A Hanna HI700 reads ammonia-nitrogen. Total ammonia = reading x 1.214 (17.03/14.01). Not owned.

kactoily.name: Kactoily 7-in-1 probe
kactoily.note: Continuous probe. Reef-oriented: its salinity and SG readings carry no information in freshwater. Ignore them.

smartlife.name: SmartLife app (Tuya)
smartlife.note: The same sensor, read through the phone app. Has a History view the CLI does not. No battery tile - an unreported datapoint, not a dying sensor.

hi735.name: Hanna HI735 (GH)
hi735.note: 0-350 ppm as CaCO3. Never substitute the marine checkers HI755/HI772/HI781/HI782 - their dye chemistries need seawater ionic strength.

hi775.name: Hanna HI775 (KH)
hi775.note: 0-500 ppm as CaCO3. Same marine-checker warning as the HI735.

advatec.name: Advatec freshwater liquid kit
advatec.note: The reference for nitrogen. Judge colour in neutral daylight against white - warm low sun shifts every tube orange. For pH prefer the calibrated probe. The ammonia scale runs yellow (0) to green (high), opposite to nitrite and nitrate.

bacnunn.name: BACNUNN 9-in-1 strips
bacnunn.note: A screen, not a measurement. No ammonia pad exists. The pH pad read 6.2 or below against a calibrated probe's 6.86 - demonstrably low. Still the only thing here that measures chlorine, copper and iron. Hold flat 30-60 s and read in the window.

observed.name: Observed / reported
observed.note: A value someone stated without naming an instrument. Treat as provisional.

prime.name: Seachem Prime

emergency.note: ammonia or nitrite emergency; both products are forgiving

change-water.note: dose the new water, not the tank

prime.note: Removes chlorine and chloramine, binds heavy metals, temporarily complexes ammonia and nitrite for about 24-48 h. Re-dose within that window if the cause persists.

stability.name: Seachem Stability

days2-7.note: label is 5 mL per 20 gal after day 1

stability.note: Nitrifying and facultative bacteria. Use after adding livestock, replacing or heavily rinsing media, cycling, or antibacterial exposure. Skip it when ammonia and nitrite read 0 and nitrate is present - the colony is self-sustaining.

melafix.name: API Melafix

with-shrimp.note: many keepers halve it with shrimp present

melafix.note: 1% melaleuca oil. Invert-safe at label dose, but efficacy is weakly supported and the surface film cuts gas exchange - which matters more here than usual, because surface agitation does both the oxygenation and the evaporative cooling.

neocaridina.name: Neocaridina davidi
notes: Below about 4 dGH there is not enough dissolved calcium to calcify a new cuticle. Presents as the white ring of death - a split behind the carapace, with no prior warning.
Copper is toxic in the low tens of ppb. They use hemocyanin, so copper is structural, not incidental.
A rapid GH rise is its own osmotic event. Walk changes up over days, do not fix them in one session.

guppy.name: Poecilia reticulata
notes: Prefers harder water than Neocaridina. In a shared tank the shrimp set the ceiling.
Shock presents over 12-36 h, not immediately.
Mixed sexes give fry within weeks and a compounding bioload.

otocinclus.name: Otocinclus sp.
notes: Shoaling. A lone one hides, grazes less, and gives no group behaviour to compare against - the belly check is then the only health signal.
Easily confused with a juvenile pleco. A common pleco reaches 30 cm and would outgrow a 25-gallon tank entirely.

mystery_snail.name: Pomacea diffusa
notes: Large, heavy feeders and heavy waste producers.
Needs at least an inch of headspace above the waterline to breathe, and an escape-proof lid. They climb.
Takes sinking vegetable pellets, blanched zucchini or spinach.
Shell erosion below about 7.0 pH with thin KH is faster than they can lay carbonate down. Existing damage never heals.

nerite.name: Vittina waigiensis
notes: Will not breed in freshwater - larvae need brackish water.
Refuses prepared food; grazes biofilm. A young setup carries thin biofilm, so judge by animal condition rather than assuming they are fed.
Place right-side up on rock, wood or glass after a transfer. They climb and escape.

spectator_ions.note: A trend line, not a concentration. GH and KH are ppm CaCO3 equivalents, not dissolved mass; the calcium in GH is largely the same ion paired with the bicarbonate in KH, so subtracting both double-counts; and conductivity-derived TDS under-reads Ca2+/HCO3-. What it is good for: if GH and KH hold steady and this climbs, something that is not hardness is accumulating. Answer that with a water change, never with an additive.

dilution.note: The same fraction applies to GH and KH, which is why change water should be matched rather than pure. A 15% pure-distilled change drops hardness 15% in one step.

target_defaults._comment: Seeds for a new tank. Per-tank targets are instance data and live in tanks.json, because they are a keeper's decision, not a species fact.
